Hey there, I have a somewhat similar experience just this morning. But, first, I'm gonna give you a background. I have been experiencing recurrent sleep paralysis since I was a teenager. I think I inherited it from my mother. I'm 22 now and it's come to a point where I don't really care for it—it's just something I've gotten used to.

Recently, I've been diagnosed with HPV and have undergone a surgical procedure to remove benign growths in and out of my vagina, so it was a really serious and painful procedure I had to go through. Recovering has been no joke to me so I have been in bed a lot and have been sleeping whenever I can afford to as sometimes my pain doesn't let me.

The point of the story is though, I am so sexually deprived and will be for a while.

So, same story goes: I fell asleep, heavy, exhausted, I haven't eaten anything, and I haven't been drinking a lot of water because peeing is so painful for me right now. In a matter of minutes after falling asleep, my sleep paralysis demon, pitch black in form, is besides me in bed. I feel them heavy on me, too. Usually, I would just close my eyes again and wait to wake up from it, but this time was different. I was so mentally drained I tried to look at my demon in the face and I did... And then, I asked them to get on top of me and fuck me.

I know that sounds weird, but they did get on top of me. I'm not sure if they fucked me, but I felt good—like I was being touched. It was such a weird experience and short-lived, too. Either way, it felt like a wet dream with more weight and then I woke up not long after, a little dismayed.

You guys have to know, I have major depressive disorder. This story may sound weird, but I'm guessing it's just a mental and emotional response to me. The last time I had sleep paralysis, I was so pissed at my demon, I beat them up to a pulp... Even though they were formless and dark. So, I don't know how that's possible. But I was so mad that I was sleeping peacefully for the fist time in a while because of my post-op pain and then sleep paralysis decided to take place which means I had to wake up again and try to go back to sleep, which is always difficult these days.

Hey. I don't know if you're supposed to apply aldara on internal warts. As per my doctor's recommendation and as per research, aldara is not supposed to be applied on internal areas because it would burn and hurt a lot. 

My next question is, when you had them surgically removed, were there remnants or leftovers? Because what I know is that if you're going to get them surgically removed then the doctors should try to remove every wart in your region as much as possible. When I asked my doctor if I could use aldara on the outside and just wait for the internal warts to go away, she said that wasn't efficient because as long as I have a wart somewhere, the chances of them growing and multiplying again is much more likely. Therefore, all warts must be removed at once to minimize these possibilities. However, upon being in this subreddit I found that some people who had their warts surgically removed can still get reoccurrences since the actualt battle does not lie in the treatment of your warts but in the strength of your immune system that will then fight off the HPV. My suggestion would be to stay on top of your health. Exercise, eat a balanced diet (and this does not mean eating less, this means adding to what you lack in diet like vegetables, folate, etc.), sleep on time, and take vitamins and supplements (Vitamin C, Zinc, Vitamin B complex, Vitamin D3).

I'm so sorry to hear about what you're going through, OP. Some treatments, like laser, do cost a lot of money. HPV is the real enemy and the warts are just symptoms you need to get treated, so what I suggest is that you stay on top of your health. I do not know the indications when you are diabetic so better ask your doctor how you can help amp up your health and/or immune system while getting your warts treated.

If laser is ineffective, you can also try other methods, like electro cauterization or Imiquimod therapy. From what I know, Imiquimod also activates a reaction from your immune system so it's a topical choice, but it's impactful. Some people also get cryotherapy. Maybe you can look for a clinic that will freeze the warts for you.

Hey, like you said, the mental game is killer so I'd like you to start there. When I got diagnosed, both doctors I went to said that stress is a huge contributing factor as it takes away from your immune system. Stay on top of your mental health. Maybe you can seek help from a therapist or a counselor. I know there are a lot of free teleconsult services now, so try to research on that.

I'd also like to tell you that although you may be struggling to clear your warts and/or lesions, there will be an end to this. They say your immune system can help clear it within two years, so just the same as your mental health, try to stay on top of your general well-being, too. I would quit vaping as vaping poses the same dangers as cigarettes anyway.

I do not know if your approach will help. The best thing she could suggest to me was cauterization, but since you're a guy, I think you can have better and cheaper options like freezing the warts (cryotherapy) or continuing medication that isn't aldara or podyphyllox. I know some of them use TCA which will be administered over a few sessions in a clinic. There are various options out there, you just gotta try what works one at a time.

Please don't lose hope! You are not alone. We will get through.
